title: Pet legacy-migration test fails on a database built from master_schema.sql alone
description:
`Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent` (`unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:792`) fails on a database that was built from `sql/master_schema.sql` alone, when the syntax-check boot has not run against that database first. It passes in the local CI matrix and in `make test-all`, where the boot runs before it.

Seen twice: in S5's verification (2026-09-30, "passes on rerun") and by the reviewer of MR !21 (2026-10-04). Reproduced on 2026-10-04 at `b485062c8`.

## Repro

```bash
docker run -d --rm --name petprobe -e MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD=probe -e MARIADB_DATABASE=luminari_probe \
  -p 127.0.0.4:3306:3306 mariadb:10.11
docker exec -i petprobe mariadb -uroot -pprobe luminari_probe < sql/master_schema.sql
LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_ENABLE=1 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_HOST=127.0.0.4 LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PORT=3306 \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_USER=root LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_PASSWORD=probe \
  LUMINARI_TEST_MYSQL_DATABASE=luminari_probe LUMINARI_TEST_SKIP_SYNTAX_BOOT=1 \
  CUTEST_FILTER=Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent ./cutest
```

```text
SYSERR: Required cascading foreign key pet_save_objs.pet_idnum -> pet_data.pet_data_id is missing
1) Test_pet_persistence_legacy_schema_migration_is_idempotent: unittests/CuTest/test_database_persistence.c:872: assert failed
```

Line 872 is `CuAssertTrue(tc, first_verification)`: `verify_pet_persistence_schema()` fails right after `run_pet_persistence_migrations()` succeeded. A second run on the same database fails the same way.

## What is not known yet

Whether this is only the test's fixture (it relies on something a boot leaves in the database, such as rows of `schema_migrations` or the tables' boot-time shape), or the migrations themselves leave the foreign key out when they start from the `master_schema.sql` shape. The second would matter on a fresh install whose first boot goes through the same functions, so that is the first thing to check.

## Done when

The test passes alone on a database made from `master_schema.sql`, with and without the syntax-check boot before it, and the cause is named (fixture or migration).

title: Bagged objects stay in memory when their owner leaves the game
description:
**Defect.** When a character leaves the game, what it had sorted into its bags stays in memory with no holder.

`extract_char()` calls `empty_bags_to_inventory()` (`src/core/handler.c`). Despite its name, that function only unlinks each bagged object with `obj_from_bag()`: no `obj_to_char()` follows, and nothing extracts the object. The objects stay in `object_list` for the life of the process.

**Effect.** Memory only. Every quit, idle-out or rent of a character with bagged objects leaks them, and anything that walks `object_list` goes on visiting them. Nothing is lost from the save: the leaving save writes the bags first (`Crash_save_bags()`), and the next login loads them from their rows.

**Also in that function.** It passes bag number 1 to `obj_from_bag()` for all ten bags, so the domain transfer record names the wrong bag for bags 2 to 10.

**Fix.** Extract the bagged objects where the leaving save extracts the worn and carried ones (`objsave_save_and_extract()` in `src/obj/objsave.c`), and decide what `extract_char()` should do with them on the paths that do not save first.

Found while fixing the review of MR !20 (S13); read from the code, not measured. Not changed there.

title: otransform leaves the object on its old rnum hash chain and miscounts both prototypes
description:
**Defect.** `do_otransform()` (`src/dgscript/dg_objcmd.c`) turns an object into another prototype by reading a fresh copy of the new prototype, copying that object over the live one with `memcpy()`, keeping eleven of the live object's fields, and extracting the fresh copy. The live object comes out of it with the fresh copy's `next_in_hash` and `prev_in_hash`, while the objects on its own rnum hash chain still link to it: after the fresh copy is unlinked and freed, the old chain runs through the live object into the other chain, and the live object's later removal from the hash edits the other chain and leaves its old neighbours pointing at freed memory, which the next walk of that chain reads. The prototype counts go the same way: the live object keeps the old rnum's count and later decrements the new rnum's (`SYSERR: Attempt to decrement object count below 0`). The live object also takes the fresh copy's event list, which the fresh copy's extraction frees.

**Fix.** Move the live object to the chain of its new rnum (`remove_obj_from_rnum_hash()`, then `add_obj_to_rnum_hash()` after the copy) and carry the count from the old rnum to the new one, as `delete_object()` and `adjust_objects()` do since `8e7b0b073`; keep the live object's events, hash links and registry state with the other kept fields, as `overwrite_object()` in `src/olc/genobj.c` does. Four world triggers use `otransform` (`lib/world/trg/`).

Seen while fixing the review findings of [MR !28](https://gitlab.com/max757/Luminari-Source/-/merge_requests/28) (#17), where `otransform` gained the sheath links in its kept list; read from the code, not changed there.
